messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Incident opened: **Private Prometheus scrape failure after NetworkPolicy change**
Severity: SEV-2 (customer impact)
Customer: (redacted) Private VPC install
Signal: Prometheus targets down / dashboards blank
Owner: @Rafael Mendes

Rafael Mendes: seeing report from Support that all Redwood dashboards went empty ~30 min ago. Likely Prometheus isn’t scraping our pods.
Can someone confirm if this lines up with any recent change in the customer cluster? @Owen Phillips

Owen Phillips: yep. Customer did a “security hardening” pass and tightened NetworkPolicies this morning. After that, Grafana shows “No data” and Prometheus /targets is mostly DOWN for `redwood-*` jobs.

Sean Gallagher: got it. classic. if they went default-deny in namespaces, Prometheus can’t reach pod `:metrics` ports.
Do we know how Prometheus is deployed in their setup? In our min pack it’s `prometheus` in `observability` ns. Some customers run their own in `monitoring`.

Bruno Silva: pulling their install notes from SUP ticket — they’re using our bundled kube-prometheus-stack, namespace is `redwood-observability`. Prometheus pod label `app.kubernetes.io/name=prometheus`.

Diego Santos: can we get the failing target details? usually it’s connection timeout (network policy) vs 403 (auth) vs TLS mismatch.

Owen Phillips: from customer screenshot of /targets:
- `redwood-runtime` endpoints: `context deadline exceeded`
- `redwood-control-plane` endpoints: same
No 401/403.

Rafael Mendes: ok. so scrape requests can’t connect.
We should ask them to run:
`kubectl -n redwood-observability exec -it deploy/prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus -- wget -S -O- http://<podIP>:<metricsPort>/metrics`
But podIP is annoying. Better: `kubectl -n redwood-runtime get endpoints` and hit service.

Sean Gallagher: +1. simplest check:
```
kubectl -n redwood-observability exec -it deploy/prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus -- sh
# inside:
apk add --no-cache curl
curl -v http://redwood-runtime-metrics.redwood-runtime.svc:9090/metrics
```
(or whatever svc/port).
If that times out -> definitely NP.

Allison Grant: reminder: our default metrics service is `*-metrics` w/ port name `metrics`. Prometheus discovers via ServiceMonitor selecting `release=prometheus` label. NP breaks traffic even if SM is correct.

Tomáš Novák: do we have a canned NetworkPolicy snippet for “allow Prometheus to scrape all Redwood namespaces”? We should, because this will recur.

Diego Santos: we don’t ship one today (we rely on “don’t block intra-cluster” assumption). But we can provide recommended NP in runbook.
For immediate: allow ingress to pods on metrics ports from Prometheus namespace/podSelector.

Rafael Mendes: action plan:
1) confirm it’s NP by curling from Prometheus pod
2) if yes, provide NP example for customer to apply
3) verify Prometheus targets recover

Rafael Mendes: @Bruno Silva can you ask customer to run the curl test from Prom pod and paste output? Also ask what NPs they applied (namespace-wide default deny?)

Bruno Silva: on it.

Sean Gallagher: meanwhile drafting NP example. We need to cover multiple namespaces: `redwood-runtime`, `redwood-control-plane`, `redwood-installer` maybe.
Assuming customer uses default-deny ingress in those namespaces, we can add “allow from prom” policy scoped to pods with `redwood.ai/metrics=true` or the metrics port.
But if they did default-deny egress on Prometheus ns, we need allow egress too.

Allison Grant: + we should keep cardinality labels out of this :)
But yes, allow from Prometheus pods to metrics ports only.

Sahana Iyer: FYI smoke tests in our harness don’t include default-deny NP scenarios yet. This is a good candidate for adding to the pack validation suite.

Rafael Mendes: agreed. add follow-up.

Bruno Silva: customer response:
- They added default-deny ingress in `redwood-runtime` and `redwood-control-plane` namespaces.
- They also restricted cross-namespace traffic to “only needed ports”.
Curl from Prometheus pod:
```
$ curl -v http://redwood-runtime-metrics.redwood-runtime.svc:9090/metrics
*   Trying 10.43.17.122:9090...
* connect to 10.43.17.122 port 9090 failed: Operation timed out
* Failed to connect to redwood-runtime-metrics.redwood-runtime.svc port 9090: Operation timed out
```

Sean Gallagher: confirmed. NP blocking.
Here’s a minimal ingress allow policy to drop into each Redwood namespace that has metrics endpoints.
(They can tighten selectors later.)

Sean Gallagher:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-prometheus-scrape
  namespace: redwood-runtime
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      redwood.ai/metrics: "true"
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: redwood-observability
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app.kubernetes.io/name: prometheus
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 9090
```
Need same in `redwood-control-plane` (and any other ns with metrics). If they don’t have `redwood.ai/metrics=true` labels, switch to selecting the `*-metrics` service backing pods (or broaden to `podSelector: {}` temporarily).

Diego Santos: do we actually label pods with `redwood.ai/metrics=true` today? I don’t think so universally.
Safer for immediate recovery: `podSelector: {}` and port list, then refine.

Allison Grant: +1. We shouldn’t assume that label exists. If they’re in outage, we want minimal steps.
Alternative: select on `app.kubernetes.io/part-of=redwood` which is more common.

Rafael Mendes: let’s give customer a “get back to green” version + a “hardened” version.
Green version:
- allow ingress from Prometheus in `redwood-observability` to any pod in namespace on named port `metrics` if possible, else numeric.
But NP can’t match named ports across pods unless the port is defined in container spec; still ok.

Tomáš Novák: also note: some of our components expose metrics on 8080 (control plane) and runtime on 9090 (depending on chart). We should not assume 9090 everywhere.
Maybe best: allow to ports 8080, 9090, 9100 (node exporter?) or check ServiceMonitor config.

Sean Gallagher: right. In their ticket, runtime metrics svc is 9090. control plane metrics is 8080.
Let’s send both.

Rafael Mendes: sending customer this (via Support/Bruno):
1) Apply these two policies:

Rafael Mendes:
```
# redwood-runtime
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-prometheus-scrape
  namespace: redwood-runtime
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: redwood-observability
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 9090
---
# redwood-control-plane
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-prometheus-scrape
  namespace: redwood-control-plane
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: redwood-observability
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```
2) Re-test curl from Prom pod
3) Check /targets

Bruno Silva: sent. customer applying now.

Owen Phillips: while they apply, note: they also have a `default-deny` in `redwood-observability` namespace for egress. If that exists, they’ll need an egress allow too.

Sean Gallagher: good catch. If egress is denied, ingress allow won’t help.
Add optional egress policy for prometheus ns:

Sean Gallagher:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-prometheus-egress-scrape
  namespace: redwood-observability
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: prometheus
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: redwood-runtime
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 9090
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: redwood-control-plane
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```
(Again, tighten selectors later.)

Bruno Silva: customer says they do have default-deny egress in redwood-observability. Sending this too.

Sahana Iyer: for follow-up: we should update installer preflight to detect `default-deny` NPs + warn “you must allow Prometheus scrape traffic” and link to doc.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Add to preflight checks + docs.

Bruno Silva: update: after applying ingress + egress policies, curl works:
```
$ curl -sS http://redwood-runtime-metrics.redwood-runtime.svc:9090/metrics | head
# HELP redwood_runtime_requests_total ...
# TYPE redwood_runtime_requests_total counter
...
```
Prometheus /targets now shows UP for Redwood jobs within ~1m. Dashboards repopulating.

Rafael Mendes: nice. marking mitigated.
Any remaining targets down?

Bruno Silva: only `kubelet` targets down (unrelated, they were down before). Redwood ones are good.

Incident Bot: Status update requested by policy. Please post current state + next steps.

Rafael Mendes: Status: mitigated. Root cause was customer applied default-deny ingress/egress NetworkPolicies in Redwood namespaces, blocking Prometheus scrapes to Redwood metrics services. Provided ingress allow policies in `redwood-runtime` + `redwood-control-plane` and egress allow in `redwood-observability`. Prometheus targets recovered; Grafana dashboards repopulated.
Next steps: document recommended NP snippets for Private minimum pack, add installer preflight warning for default-deny NP, and add validation scenario in smoke tests.

Tomáš Novák: can we also update alert annotations? when scrape fails we currently page “No data” but no guidance. add “check NetworkPolicies / service connectivity” + link to runbook section.

Allison Grant: agreed. also: we should ensure metrics ports are consistent across components (or at least documented) to make NP allowlists less painful.

Sean Gallagher: follow-ups I’m capturing:
- Docs: add “NetworkPolicy allowlist for Prometheus scrapes” section under Private observability day-2
- Installer: detect default-deny in Redwood namespaces + prompt with example policies
- Smoke tests: include default-deny NP scenario

Sahana Iyer: I’ll take smoke-test scenario. Will add a harness step that applies default-deny in runtime/control-plane namespaces and asserts our “allow-prom scrape” policy restores targets.

Rafael Mendes: thanks. closing incident.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved. Please add retro notes + action items to tracking ticket.
